paragraphs.text: Most projects begin before anyone knows exactly what they are building. There is a question to investigate, a workflow that feels awkward, a dataset that might explain something, or a report that needs to exist. Choosing a framework is often not the first useful decision.

paragraphs.text: Starter gives that early work a home. The initial brief names an intended outcome. A handful of folders separate context, working material, and deliverables. The rest can emerge through use. A research project does not inherit an application shell; a small feature experiment does not need the architecture of a platform.

paragraphs.text: The same principle applies once the work becomes substantial. Add a folder when it has something to hold. Add a dependency when it enables a real check or capability. Keep the first result small enough that someone can inspect it and decide what should happen next.

paragraphs.text: A capable agent still needs to know what success means, where the relevant information lives, and how to observe the result of an action. When any of those are missing, repeating the instruction is unlikely to fix the underlying problem.

paragraphs.text: That is the useful idea behind harness engineering: improve the environment around the agent. In the OpenAI account, that includes tools for running and observing an application, repository knowledge, automated checks, and review loops. The specific environment matters. Its results cannot be transferred to a new repository by copying a directory tree.

A polished paragraph may still make a claim its source cannot support.

paragraphs.text: When a check fails, use the evidence to choose the next action. If repeated attempts reveal the same missing capability or decision, make that gap explicit instead of retrying unchanged steps. A good handoff explains the state, the evidence, and what would allow progress. Confidence is not a substitute for any of them.

paragraphs.text: Not every preference needs a rule, and not every rule needs a script. Start with the constraints that protect the meaning of the work: original inputs stay intact, sensitive data stays out of Git, important claims retain provenance, and a change respects its agreed scope.

paragraphs.text: When a failure repeats, an executable check may be the smallest lasting fix. It might validate an input schema, prevent a forbidden dependency, or catch a misleading export. Good failure messages explain how to repair the problem. The purpose is to reduce recurring friction, not to accumulate a library of hypothetical safeguards.
